method: Cached Whisper Tiny; actual final recording; recognition does not replace listening

segments.text: I really need your help.
I've been trying to figure out how to say that without making this sound like a goodbye video.
It isn't.
But I am worried when I gained 2,000 subscribers in two days I kept checking my phone.
Like, are these actual people? You found my stories. You wanted more.
I was so happy and then everything went quiet.
I kept uploading. But the views dropped.
Lately, it feels like my video is barely reach anyone.
I don't know exactly why. That's the frustrating part.
I finished a story, put it out there, and then start wondering what I did wrong.
Maybe the opening wasn't strong enough.
Maybe the thumbnail wasn't clear.
Maybe I just need more time.
I keep turning it over in my head.
And now, there's a deadline sitting in the middle of all that.
I've got about four months before the monetization requirements change in February.
For new applicants, the Watch Hour requirement for ad revenue is going from 4,000 to 8,000.
The subscriber requirement stays at 1,000.
But those watch hours, that's twice the climb.
I want this channel to become something I can keep building.
And honestly, I'm scared I won't get there in time.
But calling the channel dead feels unfair to the people who are still here.
Because you are here, I see your comments.
When you tell me you relate to a story, or leave something kind after an upload,
I was nervous about, I read that.
It means more than you probably realize.
So if you enjoy these stories, could you help them reach someone?
Watch another one that interests you.
Share one with a friend who might relate.
And tell me honestly what you'd like to see next.
I want to get better at this.
I don't want to sit here refreshing numbers and guessing.
I'm grateful for you.
I really am.
I'm just worried.
And I didn't want to keep pretending I wasn't.
I still have stories I want to tell.
I hope you'll be here for them.
